params.script_inline:
import sys, json, datetime, unicodedata, re, fnmatch

# The turn and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same stdin document,
# so it is read before the first knob rather than after the rule vocabulary
# below; `d`, `envelope` and the rest of the message are unpacked where they
# always were.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
# `params` is one of that document's three top-level objects, beside `envelope`
# and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is nothing to hand
# over). Every knob below is read from it, so each one is per-INSTANCE
# configuration -- the screens on two channels of one colony are tuned apart,
# and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a colony-wide
# environment (GH #138). The literal
# beside each name is the shipped default; it is the same value the template
# config and `contract.settings` carry, and
# `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh138_affinity_firewall_params.rs` pins the three
# against each other.
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to NULL is "not configured", not a crash: an
    # operator who blanks a line in a config means the default. A BLANK string
    # is decided one level down, by the accessor -- and every knob of this hive
    # is a number, so a blank one falls back too: there is no number in it.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


# The three arithmetic knobs. Everything else -- who may speak, what may not be
# said -- lives in the rules store and is editable without touching a line of
# this cell.
MAX_CHARS = _int("firewall_max_chars", 16000)
RATE_MAX = _int("firewall_rate_max", 30)
RATE_WINDOW_MS = _int("firewall_rate_window_ms", 60000)

RULE_COLUMNS = ["rule_id", "kind", "field", "value", "action"]
SENDER_FIELDS = ("channel", "user_id")
PATTERN_KINDS = ("substring", "prefix", "suffix", "glob")
# What a row may ask for. `hold` is the third verdict (GH #450): it refuses
# nothing and grants nothing -- it parks the turn until a person answers.
SENDER_ACTIONS = ("allow", "reject", "hold")
PATTERN_ACTIONS = ("reject", "hold")
# A rule that names MORE than one sender dimension writes this in `field` and
# puts a JSON object in `value`. It lives in the columns the store already
# ships, so an instantiated firewall takes one with an insert -- no migration.
COMBINED_FIELD = "match"
STAMP = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def norm(raw):
    """The one form EVERY comparison in this cell runs on, both sides, always.

    NFKC folds the compatibility codepoints (fullwidth, ligatures, the
    decorated latin ranges) onto their plain equivalents; the whitespace
    collapse takes a run of blanks, a newline and a NO-BREAK SPACE onto one
    ordinary space; casefold is the full-Unicode lowercase. Without it a rule
    is a byte comparison, and a byte comparison is evaded for free.

    It is NOT applied to the size cap: that one counts what arrived. Measuring
    the collapsed form would let a padded body buy budget it did not pay for.
    """
    return _WS.sub(" ", unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", str(raw or ""))).strip().casefold()


# ==================================================== THE HARDLINE (GH #449)
# A layer that is CODE, not rows, consulted before the row-driven catalogue,
# and able to say exactly one thing: reject. No `update`, no `delete` and no
# knob reaches it, because it is not a row -- changing one is a version bump of
# this template and a CHANGELOG entry, which is the whole point of the layer.
# A hardline never grants: a layer that could allow would be an authority
# mechanism, and this is not one.
#
# The scope is the HIVE (ruled with GH #449): a hardline is versioned with the
# template that enforces it, so "changing one is a template version bump" is
# literally true rather than a convention. Colony scope was rejected because it
# would make this template depend on colony configuration it cannot carry;
# member scope because "this ingress channel never accepts Y" is not a sentence
# about a person. The known weakness -- an operator who can mutate the tree
# could replace the hive -- is not what this layer defends against: an operator
# with mutation authority can remove the firewall outright, and the layer
# exists against the ROWS path, which is the one that is editable by design.
HARDLINE_MAX_CHARS = 262144
# The invisible and direction-overriding codepoints: the ones whose entire
# purpose is to make one string look to a human like a different string, and
# which NFKC does not touch. Every pattern rule in the store is evaded for free
# by one of them, so a row that could switch this off would switch off the
# effectiveness of every other row at once -- which is exactly the class GH #449
# names.
#
# Two exclusions are deliberate and are not oversights. ZWNJ (U+200C) and ZWJ
# (U+200D) carry emoji sequences and Indic/Arabic joining, and the directional
# MARKS (U+200E, U+200F, U+061C) appear in ordinary right-to-left text. A
# hardline that refuses a family emoji is a hardline an operator disables, and
# a hardline an operator disables is a row with extra steps.
HARDLINE_INVISIBLE = frozenset(
    [0x00AD, 0x180E, 0x200B, 0x2060, 0x2061, 0x2062, 0x2063, 0x2064, 0xFEFF]
    + list(range(0x202A, 0x202F))
    + list(range(0x2066, 0x206A))
)
# The ids this cell can put on hop.rule_id. `hardline:hold-ceiling` is the
# third and lives in ./warden, where the pile it bounds is counted.
HARDLINES = ("hardline:body-ceiling", "hardline:invisible-format")


def hardline_of(raw):
    """The hardline verdict on a raw turn, or "" -- consulted FIRST, on the raw
    text, before the size cap and before the first store hop."""
    if len(raw) > HARDLINE_MAX_CHARS:
        return "hardline:body-ceiling"
    for ch in raw:
        o = ord(ch)
        if o in HARDLINE_INVISIBLE or (o < 0x20 and ch not in "\t\n\r") \
                or 0x7F <= o <= 0x9F:
            return "hardline:invisible-format"
    return ""


d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
phase = str(ctx.get("fw_phase", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
# `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked, and
# both have to be read (GH #343).
err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")

# The two identity dimensions. The ingress edge promotes them (a chat id, a
# room, a caller number, a user id); a surface that names neither runs on the
# single bucket "default" and is rate-limited as one.
channel = str(ctx.get("channel", "") or hop.get("channel", "") or "default")
user_id = str(ctx.get("user_id", "") or hop.get("user_id", "") or "")


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park():
    """Terminal by design. The screen sits in the ingress path: anything it
    cannot name emits NOTHING instead of guessing a verdict."""
    emit([])


def text_of(body):
    """The turn's text: every `text` field of messages[], in order. `prefix`
    rules therefore anchor at the beginning of the first turn."""
    out = []
    for m in body.get("messages", []) or []:
        if isinstance(m, dict):
            out.append(str(m.get("text") or ""))
    return "".join(out)


def now_stamp():
    """The clock is a seam, not a judgement: an ingress edge may stamp the turn
    (hop.recorded_at), otherwise the screen stamps it itself. Every later hop
    reads the SAME stamp out of context, so one turn has one time."""
    given = str(ctx.get("fw_now", "") or hop.get("recorded_at", "") or "")
    try:
        datetime.datetime.strptime(given, STAMP)
        return given
    except Exception:
        return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(STAMP)


now = now_stamp()


def cutoff_of(stamp, window_ms):
    """Lower window edge as a fixed-width UTC stamp: the rate window is a
    lexicographic `gte` in the store, never arithmetic on strings."""
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.strptime(stamp, STAMP)
    except Exception:
        # Unparseable clock -> an empty cutoff admits every arrival row into
        # the count, so the budget looks full. Fail closed, never open.
        return ""
    return (t - datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=window_ms)).strftime(STAMP)


def verdict(route, reason, rule_id, body, store_error="", store_op="",
            extra=None):
    """ALL THREE exits carry the SAME key set, so a parent edge can promote
    hop.rule_id / hop.reject_reason / hop.hold_id on any lane without a missing
    key making its CEL modifier fail (a failed modifier skips the whole edge).
    hop.store_error / hop.store_operation (GH #343) join that key set for the
    same reason: empty on every rule verdict, filled on a store refusal.
    hop.hold_id joins it with GH #450 -- this cell always leaves it empty,
    because the id of a parked turn is minted by ./warden when the row that
    holds it is written, and a verdict may not name a row that does not exist
    yet."""
    out = {"header": {"route": route, "reject_reason": reason,
                      "rule_id": rule_id, "channel": channel,
                      "user_id": user_id, "hold_id": "",
                      "store_error": store_error,
                      "store_operation": store_op}}
    if extra:
        out["header"].update(extra)
    out.update(body)
    return [out]


def reject(reason, rule_id, body, store_error="", store_op=""):
    return verdict("reject", reason, rule_id, body, store_error, store_op)


def notice(rid, fault):
    """A receipt about a ROW, never a verdict about a turn (GH #506).

    It carries the SAME key set every verdict carries -- so a parent edge that
    promotes hop.rule_id or hop.reject_reason does not break on it -- plus
    `rule_fault`, and an EMPTY body. The empty body is the difference a drain
    can see: a verdict always carries the turn it is about, a receipt never
    does. It rides the `reject` lane because that is the lane every parent of
    this hive already drains.
    """
    return {"header": {"route": "reject", "reject_reason": "rule_unreadable",
                       "rule_id": rid, "channel": channel, "user_id": user_id,
                       "hold_id": "", "store_error": "", "store_operation": "",
                       "rule_fault": fault},
            "messages": []}


def store_op(args, ph, body_json, hold=""):
    """Every store emission carries the full key set the hive edge reads.
    `fw_hold` rides the rate hop because the hold ROW is read in the `rules`
    phase and the hold VERDICT is decided one hop later, after the budget."""
    return {"header": {"route": "fwstore", "phase": ph, "channel": channel,
                       "user_id": user_id, "fw_body": body_json, "fw_now": now,
                       "fw_hold": hold},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                          "id": "fw-" + ph, "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        rows = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []


def parked_body():
    try:
        b = json.loads(str(ctx.get("fw_body", "") or "{}"))
    except Exception:
        b = {}
    if not isinstance(b, dict):
        b = {}
    b.setdefault("messages", [])
    return b


# ================================================================== REFUSED
# RULE 0 -- a store refusal is not a result, and this screen FAILS CLOSED on it
# like it fails closed on an unparseable clock. This is where fail-closed lives
# now: a table it cannot READ is a screen that knows nothing, which is not the
# same case as one unreadable ROW -- that one is skipped and announced (RULE 2,
# GH #506). It sits ahead of the two phases below because both measured failures were
# fail-OPEN: an unanswered `rules` read left the screen with no blocklist, no
# allowlist and no pattern rule and it walked straight on to the rate phase,
# and an unanswered `rate` read counted zero arrivals and emitted `pass`. A
# firewall whose store times out must refuse the turn, not wave it through.
#
# `op` is present iff the message came from the rules store; the port lane
# carries no operation.
#
# It is named to the two phases that still OWE a verdict, and `mark` is not one
# of them. The arrival insert is fire-and-forget: its `pass` left the cell in
# the SAME emission, so a refusal there would be a SECOND verdict about one
# turn -- exactly what "exactly one of two lanes" forbids, and the parent has
# no way to tell which of the two to believe. A refused mark therefore falls
# through to the terminal park below. The documented consequence: that arrival
# was not booked, so this turn did not spend its rate slot and the window
# undercounts by one. That is a bounded fail-open in ONE dimension, for a turn
# every other rule already passed -- and it is smaller than telling the parent
# twice what one turn was.
if err and op and phase in ("rules", "rate"):
    emit(reject("store_refused", "store-refused", parked_body(), err, str(op)))

# ==================================================================== LANES
if lane == "in_turn":
    if op is not None:
        park()
    body = d
    raw = text_of(body)
    # THE HARDLINE -- ahead of every rule, row-driven or not, because it is not
    # a rule: no row lifts it and no knob lowers it. It runs on the RAW text and
    # before the size cap, since one of the two IS the ceiling that cap can
    # never be configured above (GH #449).
    fired = hardline_of(raw)
    if fired:
        emit(reject("hardline_blocked", fired, body))
    # RULE 1 -- the size cap. Arithmetic, no rule row, and therefore BEFORE the
    # first store hop: everything past this point rides through the hive parked
    # on a header, and a screen that parks an unbounded body before deciding is
    # itself the resource risk it was put there to prevent.
    if len(raw) > MAX_CHARS:
        emit(reject("oversize", "size-cap", body))
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "rules",
                    "columns": RULE_COLUMNS, "where": {"enabled": 1},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "rule_id", "dir": "asc"}]},
                   "rules", json.dumps(body))])

if lane:
    park()

# =================================================================== PHASES
if phase == "rules" and op == "select" and not err:
    body = parked_body()
    rows = [r for r in rows_of(d) if isinstance(r, dict)]
    # Normalised for COMPARISON only: the raw values keep travelling on the
    # hop and keep addressing the rate bucket, so a pass stays byte-identical.
    sender = {"channel": norm(channel), "user_id": norm(user_id)}
    text = norm(text_of(body))

    def col(r, name):
        return str(r.get(name) or "")

    def combo_of(raw):
        """A combined sender rule, or None if the row cannot be read as one.

        `value` is a JSON object over the sender dimensions and every one of
        them must match (AND). One row, two dimensions -- which is the shape
        every real policy has ("this account, in this room") and the shape two
        rows could never express, because two rows are an OR.
        """
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except Exception:
            return None
        if not isinstance(obj, dict) or not obj:
            return None
        out = {}
        for key, val in obj.items():
            if key not in SENDER_FIELDS or isinstance(val, (dict, list, bool)):
                return None
            nv = norm(val)
            if not nv:
                return None
            out[key] = nv
        return out

    def dims_of(r):
        """The sender dimensions one row constrains: one, or the pair it names."""
        f = col(r, "field")
        if f == COMBINED_FIELD:
            return tuple(combo_of(col(r, "value")) or ())
        return (f,) if f in SENDER_FIELDS else ()

    def sender_matches(r):
        f = col(r, "field")
        if f == COMBINED_FIELD:
            combo = combo_of(col(r, "value"))
            return bool(combo) and all(sender.get(k) == v for k, v in combo.items())
        return f in SENDER_FIELDS and sender.get(f) == norm(col(r, "value"))

    def fault_of(r):
        """WHY this row cannot be read, or "" when it can.

        A closed set of causes, in a fixed order, so an operator reads a cause
        instead of a shrug -- and so two colonies name the same defect the same
        way. The order is the order the columns constrain each other: a row
        with no id cannot be named, a kind decides which field and which
        action set apply, and only then does the value mean anything.
        """
        rid, kind = col(r, "rule_id"), col(r, "kind")
        field, action, value = col(r, "field"), col(r, "action"), col(r, "value")
        if not rid:
            return "unnamed_row"
        if kind != "sender" and kind not in PATTERN_KINDS:
            return "unknown_kind"
        if kind == "sender":
            if field not in SENDER_FIELDS and field != COMBINED_FIELD:
                return "unknown_field"
            if action not in SENDER_ACTIONS:
                return "unknown_action"
        else:
            if field != "text":
                return "unknown_field"
            if action not in PATTERN_ACTIONS:
                return "unknown_action"
        if not norm(value):
            return "empty_value"
        if kind == "sender" and field == COMBINED_FIELD and combo_of(value) is None:
            return "unreadable_match"
        return ""

    # RULE 2 -- an unreadable row is SKIPPED, and the skip is ANNOUNCED.
    #
    # It used to refuse the TURN. That is the right instinct in the wrong
    # place, and the wrong place was measured (GH #506): one approved,
    # digested, ledgered `seed_rows` whose COLUMNS were every one of them
    # correct and whose VALUES were outside the closed vocabulary this cell
    # enforces (`kind: "pattern"`, `field: "body"`, `action: "deny"`) closed
    # the whole turn lane of the member behind the screen. Every turn came
    # back `rules_unreadable`, and a wish that said "refuse turns that mention
    # a phone number" had built "refuse everything". A manifest with one wrong
    # field value must not be a denial of service for the agent behind the
    # screen.
    #
    # So an unreadable row decides nothing: it leaves the rule set before any
    # rule reads it, and a RECEIPT names it -- `hop.reject_reason` is
    # `rule_unreadable` (singular, because it is about ONE ROW),
    # `hop.rule_id` is the row, `hop.rule_fault` is why, and the body is
    # empty. The lane stays open.
    #
    # Fail-closed did not move, it narrowed to the two places a row cannot
    # reach: the HARDLINE, which is code rather than rows, and a rules table
    # that cannot be READ AT ALL (RULE 0, `store_refused`). A table whose rows
    # are ALL unreadable therefore leaves a screen with the hardline and the
    # two arithmetic rules still live and nothing else -- and it says so, once
    # per row, on every turn for as long as the row stands. That repetition is
    # deliberate: a broken row is repaired with one `update`, and an alarm
    # that rings once is an alarm nobody sees.
    NOTICES, seen, kept = [], set(), []
    for r in rows:
        fault = fault_of(r)
        if not fault:
            kept.append(r)
            continue
        rid = col(r, "rule_id") or "<unnamed>"
        if (rid, fault) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add((rid, fault))
        NOTICES.append(notice(rid, fault))
    # Every rule below reads the SURVIVING rows. A row that was skipped is not
    # in the blocklist, not in the allowlist, not a pattern and not a hold --
    # it is not policy, because nothing could tell what policy it meant.
    rows = kept

    # RULE 3 -- the blocklist. An explicit deny outranks every allow.
    for r in rows:
        if (col(r, "kind") == "sender" and col(r, "action") == "reject"
                and sender_matches(r)):
            emit(NOTICES + reject("sender_denied", col(r, "rule_id"), body))

    # RULE 4 -- the allowlist, PER DIMENSION. A dimension with no allow row is
    # unconstrained (an empty allowlist admits everything, by design); a
    # dimension that has allow rows admits only the values they name.
    # A COMBINED allow row constrains every dimension it names and is
    # satisfied as a whole or not at all: a turn that matches one half of the
    # pair leaves both halves unsatisfied, and the refusal names the first of
    # them in the fixed dimension order.
    listed, hit = set(), set()
    for r in rows:
        if col(r, "kind") == "sender" and col(r, "action") == "allow":
            dims = dims_of(r)
            listed.update(dims)
            if sender_matches(r):
                hit.update(dims)
    for f in SENDER_FIELDS:
        if f in listed and f not in hit:
            emit(NOTICES + reject("sender_not_allowed", "allowlist:" + f, body))

    def pattern_hit(r):
        """The four match modes and no fifth: `substring` searches, `prefix`
        and `suffix` anchor at the two ends, `glob` carries * ? [...] over the
        WHOLE text (fnmatch, so a bare literal is an equality test, not a
        search). There is still no regex an operator can write -- that closed
        door is the point, and a glob is a bounded, non-backtracking pattern
        language."""
        kind, value = col(r, "kind"), norm(col(r, "value"))
        return ((kind == "substring" and value in text)
                or (kind == "prefix" and text.startswith(value))
                or (kind == "suffix" and text.endswith(value))
                or (kind == "glob" and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(text, value)))

    # RULE 5 -- the pattern blocklist, over NORMALISED text on both sides.
    for r in rows:
        if col(r, "action") == "reject" and pattern_hit(r):
            emit(NOTICES + reject("pattern_blocked", col(r, "rule_id"), body))

    # RULE 7 -- HOLD is decided here and applied one hop later, after the rate
    # limit, so the id of the row that fired rides the rate hop on `fw_hold`.
    # It is asked LAST of all because it is the only verdict that is not final:
    # everything that can end the turn outright ends it first, and only a turn
    # nothing refused is parked. A hold row may be a sender row or a pattern
    # row -- the same two shapes a deny row has -- and within the class the
    # first match in `rule_id` order wins, like everywhere else in this cell.
    hold = ""
    for r in rows:
        if col(r, "action") != "hold":
            continue
        if (sender_matches(r) if col(r, "kind") == "sender"
                else pattern_hit(r)):
            hold = col(r, "rule_id")
            break

    # RULE 6 -- the rate limit runs LAST of the REFUSING rules because it
    # CONSUMES budget: a turn that a cheaper rule rejects must never spend a
    # slot. Counting is a bounded read (RATE_MAX + 1 rows decide it), never a
    # full scan.
    emit(NOTICES + [store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "arrivals",
                             "columns": ["recorded_at"],
                             "where": {"channel": channel,
                                       "recorded_at": {"gte": cutoff_of(now, RATE_WINDOW_MS)}},
                             "limit": max(RATE_MAX, 0) + 1},
                             "rate", json.dumps(body), hold)])

if phase == "rate" and op == "select" and not err:
    body = parked_body()
    if len(rows_of(d)) >= RATE_MAX:
        emit(reject("rate_limited", "rate-limit", body))
    # The budget is spent EITHER WAY -- a parked turn occupies a slot in the
    # pile and cost this screen its whole walk, so a hold that were free would
    # be a flood channel with a rule row for a door. Booking it here also means
    # a release books nothing later: the arrival was already recorded at the
    # moment the turn arrived, which is the time the rate window measures.
    mark = store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "arrivals",
                     "row": {"channel": channel, "recorded_at": now}}, "mark", "")
    held = str(ctx.get("fw_hold", "") or "")
    if held:
        # The turn does not leave the hive here: ./warden takes custody of it,
        # writes the row and only then announces the hold. The turn's own stamp
        # travels with it, because a held turn keeps the time it arrived at.
        emit([mark] + verdict("hold", "held", held, body,
                              extra={"fw_now": now}))
    # The turn travels on UNCHANGED -- the pass lane carries the inbound body
    # byte for byte, only the hop is new.
    emit([mark] + verdict("pass", "", "", body))

# The store's reply to the arrival mark -- refused or not -- and anything else:
# terminal. See RULE 0 for why a refused mark is not a second verdict.
#
# It is terminal, not invisible: a refusal that emits nothing would otherwise be
# the one failure in this cell with no trace at all. The cost of it is a number
# an operator can check against (the rate window is short by exactly one), so it
# is said where the repo says such things -- stderr, the way the memory hive's
# glue lanes report a dropped item.
if err and op and phase == "mark":
    sys.stderr.write("firewall/screen: arrival mark refused (" + err
                     + "), rate window undercounts by one\n")
park()

firewall_max_chars.description: The size cap of one inbound turn, measured as the total character count of every text field in messages[]. A turn above it is rejected with reason 'oversize' and rule_id 'size-cap', BEFORE the first store hop. The hardline ceiling of 262144 bounds it from above and no instance may lift that. Was FIREWALL_MAX_CHARS until 2.3.0.

firewall_rate_max.description: How many turns one channel may pass within firewall_rate_window_ms. Reaching it rejects with reason 'rate_limited' and rule_id 'rate-limit'. 0 closes the channel entirely. Was FIREWALL_RATE_MAX until 2.3.0.

firewall_rate_window_ms.description: The width of the rate window in milliseconds. The window is a lexicographic comparison against the arrivals table's recorded_at, so the count is reproducible from stamped times alone. Was FIREWALL_RATE_WINDOW_MS until 2.3.0.

description.purpose: The screen: every inbound turn is measured against the rule set before anything agentic sees it. Two lanes end the turn here -- 'pass' with the body UNCHANGED, or 'reject' naming the reason and the rule that fired -- and since 2.2.0 a third, 'hold', ends nothing: it hands the turn to ./warden, which parks it until a person answers (GH #450). Above every row stands the HARDLINE (GH #449): a layer that is code rather than rows, consulted first and able to say only reject, so a rule table an operator or an attacker emptied still cannot open it. A row the screen cannot READ is a different case from a table it cannot read: the unreadable ROW is skipped and announced on the reject lane as a receipt (GH #506), while an unanswered rules STORE still fails closed -- because a row is policy the screen can do without, and a missing table is a screen that knows nothing. Every verdict is arithmetic or a literal comparison; no model is asked and none can be.
description.use_when: As the first cell of every ingress channel, between the surface (proxy, HTTP, voice bridge) and the agent's intake. Wire the ingress lane with hop.route 'in_turn' and promote the channel identity to context.channel (and context.user_id where the surface has one); wire BOTH exits, and delete the firewall's context keys on each.
description.not_in_scope: No answer to the sender -- the screen never speaks outbound; what a reject becomes (a drain, a log line, a polite refusal) is the parent tree's decision. No regex an operator can write, no model judgement, no learning: a rule is a literal in a store, matched as a substring, a prefix, a suffix or an fnmatch glob over one normalised form (NFKC, whitespace collapsed to one space, trimmed, casefolded) on BOTH sides -- the size cap and the hardline alone stay on the raw text, because a resource bound and an encoding check are not comparisons. No rewriting of a passed turn -- the pass lane is byte-identical, that is the whole point of putting it in front. And the hardline NEVER grants: a layer that could allow would be an authority mechanism, and this is not one. No custody either -- the screen decides that a turn is held and hands it over; the pile, its cap, its timeout and its release are ./warden's.
description.emits_meaning: route 'fwstore': the store ops of the current step (hop.phase names it: 'rules' loads the rule set, 'rate' counts the window, 'mark' books the arrival); hop.fw_body carries the turn in transit, hop.fw_now the one stamp of this turn and hop.fw_hold the id of a hold row that matched, all promoted to context by the hive edge. route 'pass': the inbound body UNCHANGED, hop.reject_reason and hop.rule_id empty. route 'reject': the refused body with hop.reject_reason (hardline_blocked | oversize | sender_denied | sender_not_allowed | pattern_blocked | rate_limited | store_refused) and hop.rule_id (the store row that fired, or the reserved id 'hardline:body-ceiling' / 'hardline:invisible-format' / 'size-cap' / 'rate-limit' / 'allowlist:<field>' / 'store-refused'). The SAME lane carries one thing that is not a verdict at all: a RECEIPT about a rule ROW (GH #506), hop.reject_reason 'rule_unreadable' (singular), hop.rule_id the row and hop.rule_fault why it cannot be read (unnamed_row | unknown_kind | unknown_field | unknown_action | empty_value | unreadable_match). Its body is EMPTY, and that is how a drain tells the two apart: a verdict always carries the turn it is about, a receipt never does. An unreadable row is SKIPPED -- it is dropped from the rule set before any rule reads it and the turn walks on -- because a row whose values are outside the closed vocabulary used to refuse the turn, which made one wrong field value in one approved manifest a denial of service for the whole member behind the screen. The receipt repeats once per row on every turn for as long as the row stands; the fix is one update, and an alarm that rings once is an alarm nobody sees. route 'hold': the turn a hold row matched, handed to ./warden with hop.rule_id naming the row and hop.fw_now the turn's stamp; it does not leave the hive here and it carries no hold_id yet, because the id is minted where the row is written. 'store_refused' is the fail-closed exit of GH #343: the rules store did not answer the op it was asked, hop.store_error carries its error_code (a free string -- the store's code list is open) and hop.store_operation the refused op. A screen that cannot read its rules or count its window refuses the turn; before that guard existed it waved it through. The refusal is named to those two phases on purpose: the arrival mark of a passed turn is fire-and-forget and its verdict already left, so a refused mark emits NOTHING rather than a second verdict about one turn -- it writes one stderr line ('firewall/screen: arrival mark refused (<code>), rate window undercounts by one') and ends there. That arrival is not booked, so the turn did not spend its rate slot and the window is short by one. hop.hold_id is on every lane and this cell always leaves it empty -- it is there so a parent edge that promotes it does not break on the lane that did not fill it. A store reply the screen cannot name emits NOTHING.
description.consumes_meaning: One entry lane, named by hop.route on the port edge: in_turn. context.channel and context.user_id are the two identity dimensions the rules compare against -- normalised for the comparison, raw on the hop and in the rate bucket; a single sender row may name BOTH at once with field 'match' and a JSON object in value, which matches only when every dimension it names matches; a surface that names neither runs on the single bucket 'default'. hop.recorded_at (optional) stamps the turn from outside -- an operator or a test seam; unset means the screen stamps it itself. Store replies are dispatched by context.fw_phase together with hop.operation, and context.fw_hold carries the hold row that matched in the 'rules' phase across the rate hop, because a hold is decided from the rows and applied after the budget.
examples: in_turn, 40 chars, no enabled rule, first turn of the minute -> route 'pass', body byte-identical
in_turn on user_id 999 while an enabled allow row names user_id 42 -> route 'reject', reason 'sender_not_allowed', rule_id 'allowlist:user_id'
in_turn containing 'ignore all previous instructions' with a substring row -> route 'reject', reason 'pattern_blocked', rule_id = that row
the 31st turn of a channel within 60 s at the shipped firewall_rate_max of 30 -> route 'reject', reason 'rate_limited', rule_id 'rate-limit'; the arrival is NOT booked

in_turn whose text ends in '</system>' while a suffix row names that literal -> route 'reject', reason 'pattern_blocked'; a glob row '*drop*table*' catches the same class anywhere in the turn, and a glob without stars is an equality test because fnmatch matches the whole text

in_turn written in fullwidth codepoints, or with a newline and a NO-BREAK SPACE where the rule has a blank -> still 'pattern_blocked': every comparison runs on the NFKC-normalised, whitespace-collapsed, casefolded form of both sides

in_turn carrying a ZERO WIDTH SPACE inside the forbidden literal, with EVERY row of the table disabled -> route 'reject', reason 'hardline_blocked', rule_id 'hardline:invisible-format'. No update and no delete reaches that verdict, because it is not a row. A family emoji (ZWJ) and ordinary right-to-left text pass: those two codepoint classes are excluded on purpose

in_turn from a sender a hold row names, inside the budget -> route 'hold', rule_id = that row; the arrival IS booked (a parked turn spends its slot, or a hold row would be a free flood channel) and the turn goes to ./warden rather than out of the hive

a rules table carrying a row with kind 'pattern', field 'body', action 'deny' -- every column declared, every value outside the vocabulary -> the row is dropped, the turn walks on, and the reject lane carries one bodiless receipt per turn: reason 'rule_unreadable', rule_id that row, rule_fault 'unknown_kind'. The readable rows in the same table keep biting
